name: Wu Haijun
current_role: Chairman & president, Shenzhen Hasee Computer Co. (神舟电脑) and its parent Shenzhen New World Group (新天下集团), per most recent available bios
profile: Wu Haijun (吴海军, b. 1966, Rudong, Jiangsu) founded New World Group in Shenzhen in 1995, which grew into Hasee, the low-price PC and gaming-laptop maker that was China's No. 2 domestic computer brand by 2008. Hasee tried four times to list on ChiNext (2010-2013) without completing an IPO; the company remains private and still sells laptops and gaming PCs.
interesting_fact: Hasee became a household name in China in 2002 with its CCTV ad slogan '四千八百八，奔四扛回家' (take a Pentium 4 home for 4,880 yuan), a price-war move that undercut major brands.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his company, Wu was a schoolteacher in Rudong County (1984-88), then earned a master's degree in power engineering (动力工程) at Southeast University (1991-94) and briefly worked at AVIC's Shenzhen group in 1994.

public_contacts.value: http://www.hasee.com/about/contact (corporate contact page; HQ switchboard +86-755-36388585, general service@hasee.com)

notes: Very low international profile; no press/IR contact published (company is unlisted). Deep-cut bio comes from a user-edited Chinese bio site (maigoo) - double-check before use. Approach via Chinese-language letter to Hasee HQ. Current status not confirmed by 2025-26 sources.

name: Shengwei (Sean) Da
current_role: Chairman & CEO, AMC Robotics Corp. (Nasdaq: AMCI; formerly AlphaVest Acquisition Corp.); Executive Chairman, Kami Vision
profile: Sean Da is a Tsinghua- and UC Davis-trained electrical engineer who ran YI Technology (Xiaomi-ecosystem action/security cameras) as chairman & CEO from 2014 to 2021, then became executive chairman of AI camera firm Kami Vision. He founded AMC Corp. in 2021 and took it public via a SPAC merger with AlphaVest, listing on Nasdaq as AMC Robotics (AMCI) in December 2025; his reported wealth is largely those insider holdings.
interesting_fact: AMC Robotics builds AI security robots, including the Kyro quadruped robot shown at CES and Tokyo Security Show 2026, and the NovaArm system now running in a live warehouse with Sunward Logistics.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a chip designer: a staff design engineer in Analog Devices' Power Management Group (2002-05), then CTO of Rock Semiconductor and engineering director at Intersil, after a PhD in electrical engineering at UC Davis.

public_contacts.value: AMCRoboticsIR@allianceadvisors.com (Alliance Advisors IR - investors and media contact)

notes: Paper wealth from a small-cap de-SPAC (AMCI); actual value volatile. Power-electronics background makes him a plausible fit for an energy/data-center angle. Best route: Alliance Advisors IR/media contact.

name: Xu Mingbo
current_role: Chairman & general manager, Beijing SL Pharmaceutical Co. (双鹭药业, SZSE: 002038)
profile: Xu Mingbo (徐明波, b. 1964) is a genetic-engineering scientist who co-founded Beijing SL Pharmaceutical, has run it as general manager since December 1994 and later became chairman. The Shenzhen-listed company makes biotech and chemical drugs (recombinant proteins, peptides, generics); his wealth comes from his controlling stake. He still chaired the board through 2025-26.
interesting_fact: Before going into business he was a research group leader at the Academy of Military Medical Sciences, led four national high-tech research projects, published 40+ papers and won a National Science and Technology Progress Award (2nd class).
deep_cut_fact: He earned his PhD at China's Academy of Military Medical Sciences and was described as one of the first young experts in 'mid- and downstream' genetic-engineering process technology trained entirely in China; he also serves on the council of the Chinese Society of Biotechnology.

public_contacts.value: lsj@slpharm.com.cn (board secretary Liang Shujie); securities rep yitingjing@slpharm.com.cn; IR tel +86 10-88627635

notes: Low public profile, Chinese-language only. In May 2026 the SZSE publicly reprimanded the company and Xu over unrecovered trust investments (company blamed alleged embezzlement by a former finance employee) - context to be aware of, sensitive. Best route: board secretary's office.

name: Stephen J Hemsley
current_role: Chairman & CEO, UnitedHealth Group (returned as CEO May 2025)
profile: Stephen Hemsley (b. 1952) is a Fordham-trained accountant who rose to CFO of Arthur Andersen, joined UnitedHealth in 1997, and was its CEO from 2006 to 2017, building Optum into the health-services giant it is today. After serving as chairman, he returned as CEO in May 2025 to lead a turnaround; his wealth comes from decades of UNH equity awards.
interesting_fact: He is widely credited as the architect of Optum, now the largest employer of physicians in the US; in 2026 he said UnitedHealth was on track to invest $1.5 billion in AI in a single year.
deep_cut_fact: Outside UnitedHealth he has sat on Cargill's board since 2015, is a trustee of the University of St. Thomas in Minnesota, serves on the Boy Scouts of America's National Executive Board, and in 2019 founded his own investment firm, Cloverfields Capital Group.
notes: Famously media-shy; rarely gives interviews. Company under heavy scrutiny (DOJ probes, litigation) - outreach should go through UHG corporate communications. Healthcare focus, weak fit for energy/data-center unless angle is AI investment.

name: Ján Moder
current_role: Co-owner of Moravia Steel group (owner of Třinecké železárny / Třinec Ironworks) and supervisory-board member; president of HC Oceláři Třinec hockey club
profile: Ján Moder is a Bratislava-born, Nitra-raised engineer who became one of the richest people in the Czech Republic as co-owner of Moravia Steel, which controls Třinec Ironworks, Czechia's largest steelmaker. Invited in 1996 to build Moravia Steel's trading arm after its privatisation, he has long lived in Třinec, sits on group supervisory boards and presides over the town's hockey club.
interesting_fact: A Slovak living in Czech Silesia, he jokingly calls himself a 'ślónski słowiok' (Silesian Slovak) and as president of HC Oceláři Třinec oversees one of Czech hockey's most successful clubs of recent years.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, in the early 1990s, imported Polish coking coal to Czechoslovak steelworks Nová Huť, VSŽ Košice and Vítkovice; in 2002 a European committee even recommended him to take over the leadership of Nová Huť.

public_contacts.value: petra.mackova@trz.cz (Třinecké železárny press spokesperson Petra Macková)

notes: Low-key; gives occasional interviews to Czech/Slovak media (Seznam Zprávy, POSITIV). Strong energy angle: Třinec is investing in steel decarbonisation and is exposed to coking-coal/energy costs. Route via Třinec Ironworks press office.

name: John W Allison
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Home BancShares Inc. (NYSE: HOMB, parent of Centennial Bank), Conway, Arkansas; handed CEO role to J. Stephen Tipton in 2026
profile: John W. Allison (79) is an Arkansas banker who co-founded Home BancShares in 1998 and built it, largely through acquisitions, into a ~$24bn-asset bank holding company operating Centennial Bank in Arkansas, Florida, Texas, Tennessee, Alabama and New York City. He is its largest individual shareholder; he was CEO 1998-2009 and again from 2019 until the 2026 succession, and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: In Q3 2026 Home BancShares posted record quarterly net income of $129.5m; Allison's take: 'In banking some play the growth game. At HOMB, we focus on stability. Strength is no accident, it's our culture.'
deep_cut_fact: Long before Home BancShares, he became chairman of First National Bank of Conway in 1983 and chaired the executive committee of First Commercial Corp., then Arkansas's largest bank holding company (~$7.3bn assets), until its 1998 sale to Regions.
